content: Semicircular lipoatrophy, also referred to as lipoatrophia semicircularis or ribbed thighs, is a medical condition observed in humans. It is characterized by a semicircular zone of atrophy affecting the subcutaneous fatty tissue, predominantly located on the anterior aspect of the thighs. Importantly, the overlying skin and the underlying muscles remain unaffected and intact. This condition is most commonly observed in office workers. The atrophic bands, or ribs, on the thighs typically measure between 2 to 4 centimeters in height and are generally situated approximately 72 centimeters above the ground. This height corresponds to the standard height of office furniture, such as desks and chairs. The exact etiology of semicircular lipoatrophy remains unclear. However, some hypotheses suggest that it may result from localized mechanical pressure or exposure to electromagnetic fields. Further research is required to confirm these potential causative factors.
